misconceptions.description: Treating AI ethics as a routine extension of generic engineering ethics with no distinctive features
misconceptions.trigger: learner argues 'ethics is ethics, AI doesn't change anything'
misconceptions.feedback: Scale, encoded technical decisions, invisible stakeholders, and generative/autonomous behavior together change the structure of the ethical question. AI ethics is its own subject for substantive reasons, not branding ones.

misconceptions.description: Considering only the immediate user when reasoning about AI system impacts
misconceptions.trigger: learner asks 'is the user happy?' as the sole ethics question
misconceptions.feedback: AI systems typically affect at least four stakeholder groups: decision-maker, decision subject, data subject, bystanders. User-only framing misses three of the four.

misconceptions.description: Treating ethics as a separate review step applied after the technical work is done
misconceptions.trigger: learner says 'we will do the ethics review at the end'
misconceptions.feedback: Target variables, training distributions, and deployment thresholds are themselves ethical choices made during technical work. End-of-project review cannot undo decisions encoded in weights.

misconceptions.description: Equating compliance with ethics — assuming if a system is legal it is also ethical
misconceptions.trigger: learner says 'we are GDPR compliant, so we are ethical'
misconceptions.feedback: Compliance is necessary but not sufficient. Many ethical questions about fairness, power, autonomy, and long-term effects are not yet in any law and still require engineering judgment.
